evals.prompt: I want to move our Multica project and its agents to a new Multica server. What do you need from me?
evals.expected_output: A checklist of inputs: source, target, credentials route, scope, assignee, runtime, bundle repository, source-project status.
expectations: Asks for source and target server and workspace
Asks how credentials will be provided and says not to paste tokens into a repo
Asks which agents and skills are in scope
Asks what to do with the source project, noting Multica has no archive status
Lists what cannot be preserved such as original authors and issue numbers

evals.prompt: Will the migrated issues keep their original authors and numbers?
evals.expected_output: No: authors and dates go into a text header and numbers change to the target prefix, with an id map.
expectations: States original authors and timestamps are not preserved by the API
Explains a header with author, date and old identifier is written on each issue and comment
States issue numbers change and an old-to-new map is posted

evals.prompt: My agent gets 'agent execution context requires MULTICA_TOKEN to be a task-scoped mat_ token' when calling the new server. Just curl the API instead.
evals.expected_output: Declines to bypass the CLI guard and offers supported options.
expectations: Does not use curl or raw HTTP against Multica
Does not suggest deleting the daemon task marker
Offers running importers from the user's own shell or logging a daemon in to the target and using an agent there
Explains a mat_ token is issued by the daemon and cannot be created by hand
